crossRefs.note: Your words have supported him who was falling, You have made firm the feeble knees.
but I would strengthen you with my mouth. The solace of my lips would relieve you.
There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
The wise in heart shall be called prudent. Pleasantness of the lips promotes instruction.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue; those who love it will eat its fruit.
A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words, and that which was written blamelessly, words of truth.
The words of the wise are like goads; and like nails well fastened are words from the masters of assemblies, which are…
Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.
Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?
I also could speak as you do. If your soul were in my soul’s place, I could join words together against you, and shake…
So how can you comfort me with nonsense, because in your answers there remains only falsehood?”
If it isn’t so now, who will prove me a liar, and make my speech worth nothing?”
Also his wrath was kindled against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.

translations.web: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?
translations.bsb: How painful are honest words! But what does your argument prove?
translations.kjv: How forcible are right words! but what doth your arguing reprove?
translations.asv: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what doth it reprove?
